body.statement: If \(r_{0n}=n^{-a_0}\), \(r_{1n}=n^{-a_1}\), and \(r_{en}=n^{-a_e}\) with \(a_0,a_1,a_e\ge0\), then the bounded-radius regime holds for \(\bar r\ge1\), and \(\rho_n=n^{-\beta_{\kappa}}\) up to the boundary logarithm specified below. If \(B\le a_1\), weak overlap causes no polynomial deterioration. If \(B>a_1\), then \(\beta_{\kappa}<B\) holds exactly when \(0<\kappa<\kappa_{\dagger}\). At \(\kappa=1\), the additional factor is \(\sqrt{1+\log_+(n r_{1n}^2)}\), and it changes the leading root-\(n\) rate only when \(a_1<1/2\). The empty-shell exponent \(a_1+\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]\) tends to \(a_1+1/2\), so its surviving fast-tail term never worsens the benchmark \(B\).
body.justification: The critical exponent turns the rate formula into a falsifiable regime map for when weak overlap truly changes attainable accuracy.
body.gap: KhanTamer2010Irregular has tail-dependent rates but not this joint nuisance phase boundary with the empty-treated-shell exponent \(a_1+\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]\).
body.consumer: A researcher can diagnose from estimated learning-rate exponents whether overlap or ordinary nuisance interaction is the binding statistical bottleneck.
